title: John McGinn ruled out of Aston Villa vs. Tottenham with hamstring issue
content:
John McGinn has been ruled out of Aston Villa’s Premier League fixture with Tottenham Hotspur with a tight hamstring.

McGinn was not included in Villa’s starting XI for Tottenham’s visit, with manager Unai Emery making seven changes from the 1-0 first leg Europa League defeat at Nottingham Forest on Thursday.

Villa’s captain was not named in the squad and multiple sources, speaking on the condition of anonymity, state McGinn is suffering from a tight hamstring, which is a direct result of a heavy fixture schedule. There is a hope that the injury is not too serious and is a preventative measure ahead of the second leg against Forest next Thursday.

“When we are playing matches in a few days like we are playing Thursday, sometimes players aren’t feeling 100 per cent, getting tired muscular, thinking not completely fit,” Emery told reporters before kick-off.

“John McGinn, he was confident yesterday but not feeling 100 per cent, so we decided not to take a risk and he’s not going to be involved today.”

McGinn has made 39 appearances for Villa this season, scoring seven goals and registering two assists.

The midfielder has also played eight games for Scotland this term, including six World Cup qualifiers to help them reach this summer’s tournament in the United States, Canada and Mexico.

Villa welcome Tottenham to Villa Park where a win would move them closer to Champions League qualification and nine points ahead of sixth-placed Bournemouth.
